items.title: Al Tinney interviewed by Monk Rowe, Buffalo, New York, October 14, 2002
items.q: I heard this Duke Ellington thing called “Normins”... I was able to steal the right notes and orchestrate it... I’m better at transcribing Ellington than other transcribers do.

ctx.x: Yeah Gowanda. So I took it over. But when he got back I had a band. I actually had a band and they were playing stocks, but they weren’t playing them sharp enough for me. So I heard this Duke Ellington thing called “Normins” — “Snibor” is a tune. It’s Robins backwards. And anyhow it seemed simple enough to get, and I was able to steal the right notes and orchestrate it, he had the right notes. And I wrote this orchestration out, I think it took me about 15 minutes. Because if it takes me any longer I’m through…
You deserve the time to sit here and watch television, right?
